Reviewed on the cheap tier at the maintainer's instruction. This PR adds posted G-code (C rewinds written into the path as real moves) and changes what the machine check accepts for a C travel, so it is under AGENTS.md's safety floor and its review should run at the high tier; treat this pass as a first screen, not the full verdict.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (first screen; the high-tier review is still owed).

### What looks good
- Clear links are strict: a point qualifies only at the path's clearance height or radius, strictly beyond all cut reach (`crates/cl/src/cl/rotary_unwind.rs:77-83`). A path with no rapid has no link and is refused by name.
- Fewest-turns logic considers both travel ends (`rotary_unwind.rs:102-117`); a rewind only moves C back toward the travel.
- Chord count is bounded (`MAX_ORBIT_CHORDS`, `rotary_unwind.rs:155`), the step is clamped, and no unwrap/expect/panic outside tests.
- Travel is read from the machine's rotary named C, the axis `machine::check` judges (`rotary_gate.rs` `c_travel`). An unstated travel leaves the path as stamped.
- The stock-conviction test (`crates/app/tests/c_axis_unwind.rs:180-189`) places stock in the rewind's way and asserts `RapidInStock`.
- Golden: C stays in -360..360 on every block; each ring keeps its 360-degree span; the cut blocks are only shifted by whole turns; no existing golden moved.

### Local results (trial merge with origin/main bdd29e00, head 3a6ff68e)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-cl unit tests (incl. rotary_unwind) | 36/36 pass |
| camcraft-cl headless_bin | 3/3 pass |
| app c_axis_unwind | 4/4 pass |
| app c_axis_live | 4/4 pass |
| app rotary_letter | 3/3 pass |
| app machine | 33/33 pass |
| app conformance | 6/6 pass |
| app golden_cl | 25/25 pass |
| clippy -D warnings, camcraft-cl + camcraft-app, all targets | clean |

Not run: the `rotary`/`millturn` name-filter suites beyond those above, the ui suites, the `--ignored` lanes and the release tier.

### Requested before merge
1. **Rewinds are posted as feed moves, not rapids** (`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_unwind.nc`). The orbit is `G01 X20 Z5 C-348.75 F22954.2` and the retract is `G01 X20 Z5 C-360 F4000`; no G00 appears after the opening move. The PR body admits the composite rapid feed is unconfirmed on a real control (owed item 5). The orbit feed (about 22,954) also exceeds the stated X/Y/Z feed of 4000. Please either post the clearance rewinds as G00 or refuse the rewind until the feed law is confirmed, and make the machine check or post judge that feed against the stated limits. The test only asserts no warnings, so nothing currently catches this.
2. **Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset reach the post untested** (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:1221` and `:1307`). Both now pass `machine_rotaries` into `stamp_spindle_c`, so a limited-travel C can now post where it was refused before. Their clearance is the radial retract cylinder (`rmax` branch, `rotary_unwind.rs:82`), which is a different link rule and is not exercised end to end. Please add at least one end-to-end test per op, or refuse these ops on a stated C travel until they are tested.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Only C is checked for finiteness (`rotary_unwind.rs:61`); a NaN point coordinate would pass into `r` and the orbit (n collapses to 1). Consider a finite check on the points too.
- The clear-link test assumes `moves[i].from == moves[i-1].to` (`rotary_unwind.rs:87`); no check enforces this chain.
- `generate.rs` is already 3268 lines; this PR adds to it (not blocking, flagged for growth).
- The decisions file (`docs/decisions/33-c-unwind.md`) names the dropped control roll-over alternative. Good.
- Body: `Refs #33`, `Changelog:` present, no closing keyword. Good.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 5c582cd5758b7cff134e06b922ef1cb16d20af24 -->

Delta review on the cheap tier at the maintainer's instruction. This PR adds posted G-code (C rewinds written into the path as real moves) and changes posted feeds on C moves, so it is under AGENTS.md's safety floor and its review should run at the high tier; treat this pass as a first screen of the fix round, not the full verdict.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (first screen; the high-tier review is still owed). Trial merge with origin/main 4c3f7565 is clean.

### What looks good
- Blocker (e) is resolved for Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset. `stamp_spindle_c` (`crates/app/src/operation/rotary_gate.rs`, the `if unwinds` branch and the refusal below it) never calls `unwind_c` for them, so no rewind move can be emitted for those kinds. Where the stamped C fits the travel they post exactly as stamped; where it does not they are refused by name.
- The "fits already" test is the machine check's own comparison: the same `c_travel` (rotary named C), and the same 1e-9 slack as `machine/mod.rs:327-333`. A posted C that rounds past the travel is refused by the machine check at post, not passed through.
- The pin `parallel_and_offset_are_refused_by_name_where_c_would_need_a_rewind` asserts the refusal text for both kinds, the posting of the stamped path on a wider travel, and in the same test that Rotary Contour (`unwinds = true`) unwinds the same helix within the travel.
- Feed cap arithmetic in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`liveMove`, about lines 492-504) is right for a composite move: the control runs the block at F along the composite length `lcmd = sqrt(dr^2 + dz^2 + dc^2)`, so X/Z runs at F*lin/lcmd and C at F*|dc|/lcmd. The caps `F <= fmax*lcmd/lin` and `F <= liveCRate*lcmd/|dc|` are the correct inversions. Zero-length guards are present (`lin > EPS`, `|dc| > 1e-9`). `feedRateMax` is the fastest stated linear feed (`machine.rs` `fold(max)`, not a sum), and the rotary rate is deg/min from the rotary's own `speeds`, consistent with the comment there.
- Feed-cap helper `assert_feeds_within` (`crates/app/tests/c_axis_unwind.rs:79-104`) checks both parts (linear and C) of every G01 block that carries X, Z, C and F, and `a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` runs it on a slower machine. The golden blocks always carry all four words, so nothing is skipped in practice.
- Golden: `git diff --stat origin/main...pr-860-review -- '*.nc' '*.cl'` lists only `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_unwind.nc` (new file, +153). No existing golden moved, `c_axis_helix.nc` included. Max F in that golden is F6000 (the test machine's stated C rate, binding on the pure-C orbit chords), and the retract is F4000 (the stated linear feed). Both are within what the machine states.
- Hardening: `unwind_c` now checks every point for finiteness (`rotary_unwind.rs:61-62`) and checks the chain (`CHAIN_TOL` 1e-6 mm, `rotary_unwind.rs:~70-80`), with pins `a_non_finite_point_refuses_by_name` and `a_broken_chain_refuses_by_name`. 1e-6 mm is far above float dust for these coordinates (~1e-12 mm at 100 mm), and a chain break refuses by name, so the tolerance cannot pass a gap silently or block good output.

### Local results (trial merge with origin/main 4c3f7565, head 5c582cd5; uncommitted merge in the review worktree, removed after)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-cl unit tests (incl. rotary_unwind) | 38/38 pass |
| camcraft-cl headless_bin | 3/3 pass |
| camcraft-post lib | 9/9 pass |
| camcraft-post axis_direction_cli / comp / comp_plane / mch_head_search / post_engine | 3 / 9 / 3 / 2 / 33 pass |
| app c_axis_unwind | 5/5 pass |
| app c_axis_live | 4/4 pass |
| app rotary_letter | 3/3 pass |
| app machine | 33/33 pass |
| app conformance | 6/6 pass |
| app golden_cl | 25/25 pass |
| app lib `rotary_gate` | 4/4 pass (incl. `parallel_and_offset_are_refused_by_name_where_c_would_need_a_rewind`) |
| clippy -D warnings, camcraft-cl + camcraft-post + camcraft-app, all targets | clean |

Not run: the ui suites, the `--ignored` lanes, the release tier, the full app suite, and the other posts' suites (fanuc, tormach, doosan) beyond the grep below. No GUI was launched.

### Requested before merge
1. **The radial-clearance branch of `unwind_c` has no test, and Rotary Contour reaches it.** `rotary_unwind.rs:93-97`: `clear` accepts a link point on the retract cylinder (`rmax`) as well as on the axial plane (`zmax`). Every unit and end-to-end test (`rotary_unwind.rs` tests; `c_axis_unwind.rs` rings and golden) exercises only the `zmax` clearance. A Contour path whose clear links are radial would post orbit rapids at the retract radius with nothing pinning that they are the intended link. The verifier judges them, but the branch's own claim ("each only where it stands strictly beyond every cutting move's reach") is unproven. Please add one unit test in `rotary_unwind.rs` (rings laid radially, `rmax` above the cut reach, the orbit at that radius, the chain and C bounds checked) and, if it can be built cheaply, one end-to-end Contour case through the verifier. Parallel and Offset do not need it: they never call `unwind_c`.
2. **The PR still says "Refs #33" with the Parallel/Offset end-to-end gap.** That gap is now closed by refusal, so the body's owed list should say so explicitly (the refusal pin is the test). Body only, no code change.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Refusal scope (blocker e, maintainer's call): refusing Parallel and Offset where C needs a rewind is safe. It adds no rewind moves for them and keeps the path the machine check already passed, so no untested output reaches the post. Refusing both outright on any stated C travel would also be safe and more conservative (it would refuse some paths that fit today); this review does not require it.
- Owed on a real control (not blocking this slice): the composite-rate reading of F (F counted as the composite of X radius, Z and C-as-mm), the G01 orbit at a composite feed in place of a G00, and the machine check on an unwound op at document level. These stay on #33 as the PR body says.
- Other C-word posts: `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (about lines 109-114) and `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` (about line 287) write C on combined moves at the mill's F with no C-rate cap. That predates this PR and is not blocking here; worth a follow-up issue.
- `generate.rs` growth and the `rotary_gate.rs` ~1e-9 slack duplicated from `machine/mod.rs` are noted only; a shared constant would tie them together.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ff0fb3924e990280994989b9cd1bb486e455d820 -->

High-tier review (safety floor: posted G-code and rotary motion). Trial merge with origin/main d47a306b is clean. This is a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (at the cut).

### Earlier blockers, checked on this head
- Round 1, item 1 (rewinds were posted at F22954): fixed. `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` caps the composite F so the X/Z part stays within `feedRateMax` and the C part within the stated C rate. In the golden, every orbit block is `F6000`, which is the bench's C rate. A pure-C chord has `lin = 0`, so only the C cap applies and `F == C rate` exactly. The retract is `F4000`, the linear feed.
- Round 1, item 2 (Parallel/Offset reach the post untested): fixed by refusal. `rotary_gate.rs` `stamp_spindle_c` never calls `unwind_c` for them. Where the stamped C leaves the travel, they are refused by name (`... proven for Rotary Contour only, so <kind> is refused where it would need a rewind`), as a `GenError::Invalid` on the op. Pinned by `parallel_and_offset_are_refused_by_name_where_c_would_need_a_rewind`.
- Round 2, item 1 (the radial branch was reachable from Contour and untested): fixed. `unwind_c(.., radial)` admits the retract cylinder only on request (`rotary_unwind.rs:102-105`), and the gate passes `false` (`rotary_gate.rs:108`). A Contour stretch whose only clear point is radial is refused by name, with the reason given (`radial_unused`, `rotary_unwind.rs:106-110`). Pinned by `a_radial_only_link_is_refused_by_name_where_radial_links_are_not_admitted` (cl) and end to end through the gate by `the_contour_takes_no_radial_link`. The radial branch also has its own unit tests: it unwinds on the r20 cylinder and is refused at or inside the cut radius.
- Round 2, item 2 (the body's owed list): fixed. The body now says the Parallel/Offset gap is closed by refusal.

### What I checked
1. **Rewind only clear of the part.** An orbit is inserted only at a stretch start `a > 0`, at `moves[a].from`. That point was reached by a rapid and stands at `zmax` (the highest rapid Z), and only when `zmax > z_cut + 1e-6` (`rotary_unwind.rs:98-105,114`). The cut reach counts every non-rapid end plus every feed start, so no rewind lands on a cut point. Inside a stretch the C values are shifted by exactly 360·k, which does not change the part-frame geometry. The orbit's C runs from `c0` (end of the previous stretch, already inside the travel) to `c0 + 360k` (inside the travel by the fit test, which includes `open`). The travel is convex, so every orbit C is inside it too. The orbit is still judged as rapids by the verifier: `a_rewind_through_stock_is_convicted_by_the_verifier` convicts a rewind through stock.
2. **Feed.** The C section is under G98 from `liveStart` until G99 is restored in `endPreamble`, so the rewind is per-minute. Every C block writes its own F, so no modal F leaks into the plunge that follows. `assert_feeds_within` checks the linear and C rates of every G01 X/Z/C/F block, on two machines.
3. **Parallel/Offset.** Refused by name at generation, as covered above. Where the stamped path already fits, they post exactly as before (same 1e-9 slack as the machine check).
4. **Equivalence mod 360.** `shifted` adds exactly 360·k. The orbit ends exactly at the link point (`j == n` → `p`). The post rotates the tip by the C it writes and refuses any block where C and XY disagree beyond `C_TOL`, so a phase error cannot post silently. The C written is the C the machine check judges against the same rotary named C (`c_travel`).
5. **No limits, unchanged output.** An unstated travel returns the stamped path untouched (`rotary_gate.rs:104-106`). A stretch that already fits comes back unchanged (`a_path_inside_its_travel_comes_back_unchanged`). `git diff --stat` on goldens lists only the new `c_axis_unwind.nc`; no existing golden moved, `c_axis_helix.nc` included.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. The `as usize` chord count saturates and is bounded by `MAX_ORBIT_CHORDS`. The input is checked for finite values and for an unbroken chain. Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/33-c-unwind.md`, this round's radial opt-in included. No snapshot PNGs, process files or dependencies are touched. The new module has its provenance line and is 364 lines.

### Local results (trial merge with origin/main d47a306b, head ff0fb392)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-cl lib (incl. rotary_unwind) | 41/41 pass |
| camcraft-cl headless_bin | 3/3 pass |
| camcraft-post lib | 9/9 pass |
| app c_axis_unwind | 5/5 pass |
| app c_axis_live | 4/4 pass |
| app rotary_letter | 3/3 pass |
| app rotary_verify | 9/9 pass |
| app machine | 33/33 pass |
| app conformance | 6/6 pass |
| app golden_cl | 25/25 pass |
| app lathe_post / lathe_post_refusals | 7/7, 6/6 pass |
| app posting | 17/17 pass |
| app lib filter `rotary` (incl. both rotary_gate pins) | 7/7 pass |
| clippy -D warnings, camcraft-cl + camcraft-post + camcraft-app, all targets | clean |

Not run: the ui suites (no UI change), the other post suites, the motion/sim suites, the `--ignored` lanes and the release tier. The PR body reports a full batch-scope gate green on this head. No GUI was launched.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- **No stated C rate means no rewind cap.** On a machine that states a C travel but no C `speeds`, a pure-C orbit block posts `F = feedRateMax * |dC| / chord`, about 57·fmax/r. That is the F22954 of round 1, and it grows on small radii. The control clamps to its own maximum, so this is not a wrong path. Still, refusing the rewind (or capping it by something stated) when C states a travel but no rate would keep F inside the data. Worth a follow-up issue on #33.
- **A Contour with `retract_z` set below `clearance_z`.** Its ring links stand under the highest rapid Z, so none counts as clear. A multi-turn path is then refused ("no clear link"). That is safe, but it may refuse jobs a user expects to post. Worth a mention in the owed list.
- The end-to-end test drives `operation::generate`, but `check_document` on an unwound op is still owed, as the body says.
- `generate.rs` is at 3273 lines and grows by 0 net here. The 1e-9 travel slack is still duplicated in `rotary_gate.rs:119` and `rotary_unwind.rs` (`TRAVEL_EPS`) against `machine/mod.rs`; a shared constant would tie them together.
- The other C-word posts (`fanuc.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`) have no C-rate cap. This predates the PR and is already listed as a follow-up in the body.
- Body: `Refs #33`, `Changelog:` present, conventional subjects, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit. Good.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
